articleTitle: Automating the routing of medium voltage cables in electrification design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the method that will be used in developing a software tool to automate the routing of MV cable to interconnect a number of transformers on a CAD-based township map. The method proposes the use of intelligent map techniques to route the cables along roads and stand boundaries, while treating blocks of stands as impassible obstacles. This work forms part of the ongoing research at the University of the Witwatersrand to develop software tools to free electrification designers from as many repetitive and time-consuming tasks as possible.

articleTitle: Gilbert channel model parameters for GMSK on a rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we parameterize the Gilbert channel model for Gaussian Minimum Shift Keying, as used for example in the GSM cellular system, on a flat Rayleigh fading channel. The generation of the appropriate data for the derivation of the discrete channel model, is done by means of a simulation. In the simulation, we assume that the fading is slow enough such that the receiver may perform perfect carrier recovery and synchronization. We find analytical expressions for the parameters of the model as a function of the average signal-to-noise ratio (for a fixed Doppler shift), and as a function of maximum Doppler shift (for a fixed average signal-to-noise ratio) by means of a curve fit.

articleTitle: A tutorial on the basics of reed solomon and BCH error-correcting codes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A widely used method for error correction in digital communications is the Reed Solomon code, a type of BCH code. Reed Solomon and BCH codes are applications of the algebra of finite polynomial fields to the problems of how to encode the information, correct errors, and then decode to recover the information. This article is a tutorial on the methods and the mathematical fundamentals of these codes.

articleTitle: Power line carrier system on a 400kV compact delta transmission line
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper discusses the power line carrier (PLC) engineering aspects of a new configuration of HV transmission line placed into service by Eskom (the South African Power Utility). The line is of compact delta design, differing significantly from the standard flat horizontal configuration in common use throughout the country. PLC signal propagation characteristics of both the delta and a typical flat horizontal line are calculated and compared, both with one another and with measured results after commissioning the compact delta line. Predictions of the anticipated line noise level are discussed and compared to in-service measurements taken after the line had been in operation for two years. Finally overall PLC system performance predictions are compared to those observed in practice.

articleTitle: An algorithm for adaptive homophonic coding of cryptographic sources
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The breaking of most cipher systems relies on the fact that message symbols are not uniformly distributed. In this paper we introduce an adaptive homophonic source coding scheme to alleviate this problem. The adaptive homophonic coder transforms a non-uniformly distributed source into a non-deterministic, uniformly distributed message sequence. This is done by combining homophonic substitution with Arithmetic coding. The adaptive nature of the algorithm allows the algorithm to be used with an arbitrary message source.

articleTitle: Methodologies for modelling water reticulation related energy recovery systems in deep-level gold mines
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This article provides a structured methodology for the development of energy conversion models of the energy recovery systems present in the water reticulation system of deep-level gold mines. The developed models of the energy recovery systems are intended to complement models of energy consuming components. Together, these will provide a powerful, versatile tool for finding energy cost-effective configurations, schedules and tariffs. This article concentrates on the planned flow of information, modelling approach, system contexts and an introduction to the fundamental principles of existing energy recovery systems. It is concluded with the proposal and verification of different energy recovery system models.

articleTitle: H.323 direct call signalling call detail record (Data) extraction
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Abstract With the rapid expansion of the Internet and packet switched networks, combined voice and video communication via packet switched networks is becoming a reality. Two major technologies are currently implemented for real time voice and video communication over IP: Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) and the ITU-T's H.323 standard. In order to bill for voice and video services delivered via the Internet, billable information needs to be extracted from the packet flow. The H.323 standard incorporates various protocols for voice and video communication purposes the most important being the RTP/RTCP media transport protocols, the H.225 call signalling protocols, and the H.245 call control protocol. We firstly determine whether the H.323 suite of protocols contain extractable information for use in billing. This paper then shows how sufficient information can be extracted from the IP packet flow for billing and service level agreement purposes of H.323 Internet-based calls.

articleTitle: Estimates of refractivity gradient and K-factor ranges for botswana
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A presentation of refractivity gradient and K-factor variation, based on radiosonde measurements carried out over 3 years in Maun, Botswana, is reported. It is observed that the median refractivity gradient within 0-200 m height range is -20 N-units/km. The percentage of the time for which the refractivity gradient is lower than -100 N-units/km is found to vary from a high 32% in February to 13% in August. Similarly, ducting is seen to be quite prevalent in summer (23% of the time in February, and 17% in November), while it is less prevalent in winter (12% of the time in May and 6% in August). A comparison between recent ITU-R plots for refractivity gradient and ducting occurrence frequency for the region, with the reported measurements, shows fairly close agreement. When ducting values are excluded, the median K value is found to be 1.1, while the effective value exceeded 99.9% of the time, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</inf>, is 0.7. On the other hand, when all data are considered, the median value of K is found to be 1.03 while K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</inf> is determined to be 0.61.

articleTitle: A distributed call admission control protocol for DS-CDMA cellular networks
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A unique feature of DS-CDMA cellular networks is its universal frequency re-use concept In other words, neighbouring cells operate on the same frequency channels. Because of this universal frequency re-use concept, the admission of a user into the network affects the level of communication quality of all the other users. Call admission control then becomes critical and a new user will be accepted only if the additional interference that it creates does not degrade the overall communications quality of the already admitted users beyond some acceptable level. Most of the call admission control schemes that have been analysed in the literature are centralised in nature and there has not been much work done on distributed or decentralised schemes. This paper proposes a distributed call admission control protocol for DS-CDMA cellular networks. In this distributed scheme, channel access decisions are made by the mobiles based on information broadcast from the base stations. This is different from the access strategies that have appeared in the literature where call requests are processed solely by the base stations. Teletraffic performance measures that are considered are the probability of blocking calls, probability of forced termination, grade of service and outage.

articleTitle: Mitigating the EFFECTS of uncertainties in induction machine drives using quantitative feedback theory
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents a design of feedback controllers using Quantitative Feedback Theory for a high performance drive system, to overcome the undesirable effects of uncertainty within a range of machines. A parameter estimator and a power efficiency search algorithm are also presented. It is demonstrated that by accurately quantifying the uncertainty within a plant specific dynamic performance at critical frequencies can be achieved. Digital simulation results are presented to substantiate the analysis.

articleTitle: Ground voltage and ground current cancellation by coaxial cable
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The most frequent use of coaxial cable is to prevent electrical noise adding to signals passing between equipment. Ground voltage differences exist and appear in series with the signal. The screen of a coaxial cable grounded at both ends induces a voltage in the inner conductor which starts cancelling ground voltages at about 2.5 kHz and can produce -60 dB cancellation at 10 MHz. The signal current also produces a flux external to the screen, which induces a loop current through the screen and ground path. Above 2.5 kHz, the loop current starts opposing the returning ground current, redirecting it from the lower impedance ground path to the screen, thereby reducing the external magnetic field. An equivalent circuit explains the phenomena and the extreme sensitivity of coax and oscilloscope probes to short pigtail leads. Experiments and data are described which justify the theory. Remarks are made on pigtails, cable trays, and feeding power via coax.
